extracted.intended_audience: independent experts/evaluators assessing Horizon Europe proposals (and applicants seeking to understand evaluation criteria)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating Horizon Europe grant proposals against the three award criteria (Excellence, Impact, Quality and Efficiency of the Implementation), including scoring rules, thresholds, weighting and two-stage call provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Every proposal is judged on 'Excellence' as one of the three award criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: clarity and pertinence of the project's objectives; soundness of the proposed methodology (concepts, models, assumptions, interdisciplinary approaches, gender dimension where appropriate, open science practices, methods/data quality); ambition — the extent to which the work is beyond the state of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Impact' criterion assesses the proposal's potential to achieve meaningful results and make use of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: credibility of pathways to expected outcomes; suitability and quality of measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts (dissemination, exploitation, communication); scale and significance of expected outcomes (note: 'scale and significance' wording is simplified from WP2026/27 onwards). For Innovation Actions, Impact may be weighted more heavily in ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and Efficiency of the Implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well the project is planned and how resources and participants are organised to deliver it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: quality and effectiveness of the work plan; allocation of tasks/resources; capacity and role of each participant; suitability of the consortium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system (0–5) and score meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each criterion is assessed on a scale of 0–5 points (resolution of half points is noted), with prescribed meanings for each score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score definitions provided: 0 = proposal fails to address the criterion or cannot be assessed due to missing or incomplete information; 1 (Poor) = inadequately addressed or serious inherent weaknesses; 2 (Fair) = broadly addresses criterion but significant weaknesses; 3 (Good) = addresses criterion well but a number of shortcomings are present; 4 (Very Good) = addresses criterion very well but a small number of shortcomings are present; 5 (Excellent) = successfully addresses all relevant aspects; any shortcomings are minor. The page also states: 'Each evaluator must assign an integer score from 0 to 5 for every criterion independently.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold requirements for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum scores required for a proposal to be eligible for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposal must reach at least three points for each of the criteria and ten points in total. A single criterion falling below 3 out of 5 terminates the proposal's chances regardless of its total score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting variations between action types and calls
rubrics_metrics.description: How the three criteria are weighted for ranking depending on action type or specific call texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Innovation actions, the criterion 'Impact' is given a weight of 1.5 to determine the ranking. For standard Horizon Europe action types, all three criteria carry equal weight. Some specific call topics or cross-cutting priorities may specify different weightings; the call text can override the default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage calls: stage 1 evaluation and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for two-stage calls where an abbreviated proposal is evaluated in the first stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In two-stage calls, a shortened version of the project proposal is submitted at the first stage, and only the criteria of 'Excellence' and 'Impact' are evaluated, with at least four of the total five points required for each criterion at stage 1.
